result_text:
I fixed the four default scoping conventions in `ScopingConventions.java`. Nothing is committed.

- **Generated HTML pages:** the pkgdown, Doxygen and meta-generator rules now match `(htm|html|xhtml)`. They previously had `html` twice and no `htm`.
- **.NET assembly docs:** the path pattern is now `.*[.]xml`, so `MyAssembly.xml` matches. It was `.*/[.]xml`, which only matched a file named `.xml`.
- **JavaScript generated by `// Generated by …`:** the path pattern is now `.*[.]js`, so `app.js` matches. It was `.*/[.]js`.
- **Gradle JavaScript scripts:** the pattern is now `.*[-]gradle[.]js`, so `build-gradle.js` matches. It was `.*[.][-]gradle[.]js`, which only matched `.-gradle.js`.

The module compiles offline. I did not add or run a unit test, because the module has no existing tests for these conventions and I could not write a scratch file to check them with Java. I checked the path patterns with `grep -Ex` against sample names instead. The results were as intended: `.htm`, `.html` and `.xhtml` match, `.php` does not, `app.js` and `MyAssembly.xml` match, `app.json` does not, and `build-gradle.js` matches while `app.js` does not. The content patterns are unchanged.

One related bug I left alone because it is outside the four you listed: line 292, `.*/[.](css|js)[.]map`, has the same leading-`/[.]` problem and never matches a real `*.js.map` or `*.css.map` file.
